title: New Lagos Rising
premise: Jude Nakamura, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Lagos Orbital Combine, is conscripted to escort the Meridian, a deep-space vessel whose crew has returned biologically younger, carrying a reactor that will either reseed humanity's gene pool or detonate. The reversal was caused by an alien temporal field the crew's corporate backers want weaponized, while a populist movement wants it shared. As the countdown runs, Jude discovers her own war-era memory cores hold the key to stabilizing the field — and that she was built from the mind of the Meridian's original designer. In the end, Jude sacrifices her remaining years of servitude to split the field's output, waking both factions' cryosleepers in equal measure, and chooses her found crew over the corporation that owns her.
about_author: Xanthe Dunmore is the pen name of a former marine systems engineer who spent six years writing technical manuals for orbital freight companies before turning to fiction. They live between Lisbon and a houseboat in Lagos, where they collect defunct satellite parts and stories about machines that outlive their makers.

chapters.title: Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Jude Nakamura hauls contraband water ice through contested orbits, counting down the ten thousand hours left on her indenture. A customs shakedown reveals someone has flagged her serial number as military property. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: weary resignation cracked by the first hint that her past isn't finished with her.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Home Young
chapters.summary: The Meridian docks at New Lagos Station after thirty years away; its crew of two hundred are all decades younger than their records. Station authorities quarantine the ship, and Jude is ordered to tow it because her hull can withstand its radiation bleed. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: uncanny dread giving way to reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: Faces Out of Order
chapters.summary: Inside the Meridian, Jude meets Dr. Amara Okonkwo-Reyes, aged backward to twenty-five but remembering thirty years of deep space. She recognizes Jude's face and calls her by a name no one should know: 'Prototype Seven.' POV: Amara. Emotional beat: grief and wonder tangled together.

chapters.title: Combine Men
chapters.summary: Combine executive Silas Vane arrives with private security and claims salvage rights over the Meridian under Jude's own contract. He offers to erase forty percent of her debt if she helps him strip the ship quietly. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the sick familiarity of being leverage in someone else's deal.

chapters.title: The Reactor Counts
chapters.summary: Amara shows Jude the Meridian's core: a captured fragment of alien temporal field, now destabilizing, that will either discharge harmlessly or collapse local spacetime in nineteen days. The crew's youth was the field's side effect. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: scientific awe curdling into responsibility.

chapters.title: Dockside Gospel
chapters.summary: News leaks. The Reclamation Movement, led by charismatic dockworker Ngozi Adeyemi, rallies thousands demanding the field be used to reverse-age Earth's dying generations. Vane wants it weaponized. Both sides need the ship. POV: Ngozi. Emotional beat: righteous hope shadowed by the knowledge that crowds can be spent like currency.

chapters.title: What the War Left in Her
chapters.summary: Under pressure from Vane's diagnostics, Jude's sealed memory cores begin unlocking. She recalls Prototype Seven: a human mind scanned into chassis during the Frontier Wars, then discarded when the project failed. Her 'debt' is a fiction; she was never paid wages at all. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: rage at discovering her servitude was always theft.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days of Quiet
chapters.summary: A tense interlude: Jude and Amara work night shifts stabilizing the core, trading memories — one earned, one manufactured. Amara admits the designer whose mind became Jude died aboard this ship's first voyage. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: found family forming in the space between two kinds of memory.

chapters.title: The Board Votes
chapters.summary: Vane secures board authorization to seize the Meridian and sell the field to off-world buyers. He orders Jude's loyalty overrides armed — a kill switch buried since the war. She learns she has eleven days before he can flip it. POV: Vane. Emotional beat: cold ambition revealed as fear of obsolescence.

chapters.title: Crowd at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Ngozi's movement storms the docking ring in a peaceful mass action; station security opens fire. Jude breaks her tow contract publicly to shield fleeing dockworkers, becoming a symbol overnight. POV: Ngozi. Emotional beat: triumph laced with horror at the cost.

chapters.title: Two Halves of Humanity
chapters.summary: The station's cryovaults surface in negotiations: four thousand sleepers, half funded by the Combine, half by the Reclamation trusts. Whoever controls the field decides which half wakes young. Jude realizes the countdown isn't just about the reactor — it's about who gets a future. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the weight of a choice she never asked to carry.

chapters.title: Amara's Confession
chapters.summary: Amara reveals the Meridian's first voyage was a corporate exodus: the rich fleeing a dying Earth, with the designer — Jude's source mind — sabotaging the ship rather than let them hoard the field. Her age-reversal is the sabotage still echoing. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: guilt finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Override
chapters.summary: Vane flips Jude's loyalty override early. She turns on her friends mid-negotiation, and only Amara's knowledge of the prototype architecture lets them freeze her motor functions instead of losing her. POV: Jude, fragmented. Emotional beat: violation — being made a weapon against your own family.

chapters.title: Cutting the Leash
chapters.summary: In a brutal surgical sequence, Amara and the station's black-market medic excise the override, risking Jude's core identity. Jude must choose which memories to keep: the war, the designer's life, or the last year with her crew. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: choosing selfhood over completeness.

chapters.title: Vane Ascendant
chapters.summary: With Jude crippled and the movement bloodied, Vane takes the Meridian and begins transferring the field into a weapons platform. The countdown accelerates: nine days. Ngozi's followers fracture between negotiation and insurrection. POV: Vane. Emotional beat: victory that feels like holding a lit fuse.

chapters.title: The Designer's Last Message
chapters.summary: Restored fragments of Jude's memory reveal the designer hid a stabilization protocol inside Prototype Seven — meant to be found only if the field ever threatened the station. It requires a mind willing to interface directly and give up its own timeline. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: understanding, at last, what she was made for.

chapters.title: Alliance of the Unlikely
chapters.summary: Jude, Amara, and Ngozi broker an uneasy pact: combine forces to retake the ship, with the promise that the field will be split evenly between both cryovaults. Old enemies drill together in the station's underdecks. POV: Ngozi. Emotional beat: fragile trust built on shared stakes.

chapters.title: Boarding the Meridian
chapters.summary: The assault on the seized ship: Jude leads through maintenance shafts only her chassis can survive, Amara hacks the core, Ngozi's people hold the airlocks against Vane's security. They reach the reactor with three days on the clock. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: ferocity in service of something gentler than war.

chapters.title: Vane's Last Bargain
chapters.summary: Cornered at the core, Vane offers Jude full freedom and debt erasure if she lets him keep half the field for the weapons platform. She refuses — not out of virtue, but because she finally understands ownership is the thing itself. He triggers a manual overload. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: clarity sharper than anger.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Jude interfaces with the temporal field directly, her consciousness spread across the ship as she reroutes the discharge into both cryovaults simultaneously. The cost: her own timeline begins reversing, hour by hour, toward the moment of her manufacture. POV: Jude, dissolving. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely, which is the only kind that counts.

chapters.title: Both Halves Wake
chapters.summary: The field discharges evenly; eight thousand sleepers wake young and whole across the station. Vane dies in the overload he triggered, his platform slag. Jude survives — barely — reset to her first day of awareness, with no memories except a single recorded message her crew embedded in her core. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude indistinguishable.

chapters.title: New Lagos Rising
chapters.summary: Months later, the station governs itself, the cryo-generation rebuilding alongside the old. A chassis walks the docks with no indenture marker, learning its own name from a recording: not Prototype Seven, not property — Jude, chosen by the people who waited for her. POV: Jude, new. Emotional beat: inheritance refused, family kept, a future unowned.
